newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Buenos Aires province to privatise main utilities.
newsitem.headline: Buenos Aires province to privatise main utilities.

text.p: The government of Argentina's province of Buenos Aires said Thursday the province's two biggest utility firms will be privatised next July.

According to Hugo Toledo, the province's public works and services minister, electricity company Empresa Social de la Energia de Buenos Aires (Eseba) SA and and water company Obras Sanitarias de Buenos Aires will be sold in July 1997, said state news agency Telam.
"Eseba has 4,700 workers who will maintain their jobs, their positions and their remuneration, once the sale goes through," said Toledo.

Eseba, which has annual revenue of some $800 million, became a listed company in July 1990 with the province retaining a majority stake in the company. Eseba is made up of three electricity power generators, the whole high tension network for the province and distribution systems for the region's main cities.

Osba supplies drinking water to 3.5 million consumers in the province and when privatized that figure will rise by 1.5 million. The Osba concession will be for 30 years and will require a $1.5 billion investment in the service, said Toledo.
